title: How do I stop AI for coding stupid text everywhere like the public of my game is a bunch of 5 year olds?
author: Morpegom
selftext:
So basically I had AI help me code my game. Its been doing the title for a while now no matter what I do. I'm using Codex/Claude, have one account in each and both have the same issue.

Basically I wanted it to create a info pop up of any item acquisition in my game.

So the player would click the item, a pop up would appear, and there would be information on it. My prompt for it was:

"Keep the item icon, name, rarity, type and description. So the information shown would be as an example: Crowbar, Common, Weapon, Description under the card. Keep the interface clean and simple, the only texts in this info tab will be the ones I provided"

I even draw a prototype of exactly what I wanted.

Then, when it implemented, the final product was:

https://preview.redd.it/c4dpnm19uelh1.png?width=850&format=png&auto=webp&s=e155de8eb10e536607c3c6367b450a8cbeeed97a

What do you mean it added a flavor text? Since when did I ask for a flavor text? And what about "Rarity - Rare"? Like wtf? And what is "Random" even about?  


I swear to you guys: Everytime I implement any part of the UI in my game, it gets floaded with useless text. Is there any way to stop that? Maybe a custom point to this in the [agents.md](http://agents.md) skill?

comments.author: ResenhaDoBar
comments.body:
I hear you, this is the most annoying AI trait for me, what I do is have this rule for my projects:

"Do not create UI elements unless specifically asked for. Do not generate flavor text unless explicitally asked for."

This usually helps, but sometimes it doesn't. The AI always find a way to create some random fucking bullshit text somewhere that it knows I'm not looking.

replies.author: Bluetails_Buizel
replies.body: How about saying, “I’ll fill in the flavour text by myself later, you do x and y”

comments.author: thep1x
comments.body:
This has been happening ALOT lately, the over explaining has caused me to rewrite large swaths of spiced.gg and its still ongoing (if you see something I haven’t caught, let me know)  Also whats most annoying is the teat is so off base you start to question what your own intent was in the first place.    
![gif](giphy|135KrgRFPb2dZ6)

comments.author: DigitalDustChan
comments.body:
Yeah, you need to create, develop, buy, or steal a design skill. Those clankers are really good at following directions, but they have to be specified in a way they understand. Give them an example of good output. Try not to say "don't do this" too often.

Most of all you have to change your outlook on what the job is about. You're not a developer, you're a blacksmith. You pound on it with a hammer and it fixes the part you were pounding on but warps the other parts. The next thing to do is pick the next spot that needs a hammer blow and strike it there. Eventually you run out of blemishes to hammer out.

comments.author: hblok
comments.body:
If you have a specific audience and requirements in mind, that's the most important context you need to nail down from the very beginning, in your planning doc.

"This is a game for 5-year-olds who cannot read. Use icons and pictures instead of text".

If you're already heading down the wrong track, it's usually futile to try to correct course. Start over, with a detailed planning doc.

replies.author: florodude
replies.body:
No I think he's referring to the game always including flavor text that's often like an overflow of prompting. So if I said "when the user hits space it jumps. This is helpful for jumping over spikes or obstacles"

You'll get actual text on your game that will be like "space: jumps. Helps you get over spikes and other scary things!"

comments.author: florodude
comments.body: Holy shit I deal with this all the time!!! "Stop putting shitty help text. This game doesn't need sarcastic color commentary" only gets me so far

comments.author: flywheeling
comments.body:
For text editing, I often have a separate naive agent be a critic using my guidelines. I ask it write up a list of violations and hand that back to the original agent.  

You can loop this until the critic has no complaints.  

This “linting” or adversarial style has been way more effective for me than trying to give guidelines to the agent that writes the first draft. 

It helps get rid of slop signals like em dashes and negative parallels, like “It’s not just rare, it’s unique.”

Good luck with your game.

comments.author: 3tt07kjt
comments.body:
You may be overspecifying what you want or asking it to make too much in a single step. Better to give it somewhat more vague instructions.

It would be nice if we could give exact instructions and the AI follows. What happens if you give instructions that are too exact is, sometimes, you get weird results.

comments.author: Correct_Emotion8437
comments.body: I get this all the time.  I asked it what it calls this extra text and it said “bootstrap text and diagnostic text”.   Now I ask it to remove all bootstrap text and it gets rid of it.

comments.author: mongooseisapex
comments.body: Do you have a reference spreadsheet or document of every single item in the game that needs a pop up? Then the AI refers to the database and use the information on there only when making the pop up. I found that worked for me

comments.author: Fulgren09
comments.body:
It's not a question of constraining, its the nature of generative AI. Unless the data is structured, LLM is making it up each time.  You can try controlling it on the UI side, and set up item desc to have a schema, and have the specific game element map the items sort of like  
   
{ name: 'Emergency Crowbar',  
  rarity: 'Common',  
  type: 'Crowbar',  
  description: 'asdf'  
....  
}

comments.author: ContactIcy3963
comments.body: Throw in permanent memory not to gamble and hallucinate extra features not asked for.

comments.author: RedTheRobot
comments.body:
I don’t know how you are building your pop up but it really sounds like you want it to create an image for each item which is not what you should do. You should use a json or any other dataset. They give ai the example json and say you want it to build a pop up system that can support this json. Then it becomes just building the json and that’s it. 

So example prompt would something like. I want to build an item pop up system for the game. It should use this json format to fill in the fields. One the fields will be an icon for the item. The system should also support font coloring. The title of the item should be a bigger font than the rest of the text. 

Even if it generates flavor text it doesn’t matter because it is an empty text field you can remove or not fill in on the json.

comments.author: LazyAp3
comments.body: Either overspecify in your prompt (i nnow this sounds dumb but tell your idea and what you want/dont want to chatgpt and let it spit out a codex prompt) or just refine it, none of those seem like a suoer big issue to deal with manually or just tell codex/claude to change/remove it

comments.author: sicospecialist
comments.body: Every game starts with a game bible or GDD, add this as a parameter guide and rule set for your agent, and keeping a git or repository is paramount. Along with a rule sets, then the ai will have a solid reference of what your want, and update the GDD and rules often. I'm building a rather ambitious game, and it knows exactly what I expect, bot perfect, occasional bug or not exact. Good Luck!
